placements.why: This envelope's entire content is a probe whose sole function is to have the e2e suite verify and record a specific behavioral rule (reviewer enrollment on save). Nothing in the supplied (empty) strata covers testing-as-organizational-record, and the shape of the content — a memory minted purely to carry a suite assertion — makes 'proof/verification' legible as its own top-level organizational category rather than a fact folded elsewhere.
placements.title: Automated e2e assertions become the record of what the system verifiably does
placements.frame: What organizational weight does a passing e2e assertion carry as evidence of a system's actual behavior, as opposed to a design intention or a decision recorded elsewhere?

placements.title: Saving a memory as an act that quietly appoints its own reviewer
placements.frame: What does the system commit to, and what does it risk, by treating the act of saving as the act that determines who reviews?
placements.why: Src-1 states the rule the suite asserts (save enrolls creator as reviewer) as a settled decision, and src-2 frames the probe memory as existing purely to carry that same assertion — together they name a policy subject (who gets enrolled as reviewer, and on what trigger) that future envelopes about enrollment, review workflows, or suite changes will keep feeding, not a one-time fact. It sits under the newly minted Proof stratum because both segments cast the e2e suite, not a human decision, as the thing asserting and carrying this policy.
